draft.title: The eukaryotic cell cycle
card: The cell cycle is the series of events from one cell division to the next. In eukaryotic cells it has three parts: interphase, mitosis and cytokinesis.
the longest part of the cycle. The cell grows, makes new organelles and copies its DNA, so each chromosome ends up as two identical copies.
the nucleus divides. The copied chromosomes are shared out so that two nuclei form, each with a full set of the cell's DNA.
the cytoplasm and cell membrane divide, so one cell becomes two separate daughter cells. It usually follows mitosis.
draft.remember: Interphase prepares the cell, mitosis divides the nucleus, and cytokinesis divides the cell.

a.q: A cell has just finished copying all of its DNA. In which part of the cell cycle did this happen?
a.why: DNA is copied during interphase, before the nucleus divides. Mitosis is tempting, but it shares out DNA that has already been copied. It does not make the copies.
a.clue: Think about what must happen before a nucleus can be divided.

b.q: A researcher sees a cell with two nuclei inside one shared cytoplasm. Which part of the cell cycle has most likely not happened?
b.why: Two nuclei mean mitosis has divided the nucleus. The cytoplasm has not split, so cytokinesis has not happened yet. DNA copying must have happened earlier, in interphase, or the two nuclei could not each hold a full set of DNA.
b.clue: Which part divides the cell itself, not just the nucleus?
